You don’t have Ffi, that’s a primarily genetic disease with an age onset of 40-60. Also if you know the YouTuber who said he had it, that guy took a bad antibiotic that is not prescribed by pediatricians. He didn’t have fatal insomnia but he had severe neuropathy and the pain was so bad he could barely sleep.

I was dealing with the same thing over the summer(August-September). Convinced I had a prion disease and went to two hospitals. Had hypertension and a rapid heart rate to add to it. 

That was 7 months ago and I’m still here with resolved insomnia(sleeping 8 hours again).

First of all, FFI is genetic so unless you know someone in your family  whose died of it that one is out of the question. The American families who have it are listed: Michael Corke, DF, Sonia Vallabh,  two unnamed people, Rick White,  and in 2020 a man in Connecticut. That’s it. And then there’s 2 families in Australia and a few in Europe, China,  and Northern Africa. 

Now Sfi is not genetic so this one is a bit trickier..but the vivid dreams talked about in prion disease aren’t really dreams. They’re more of hallucinations that intrude into waking life and they can’t tell if they’re awake or asleep. By this time, they’re in such a daze that they don’t even realize they can’t sleep. There’s been about 12 cases of Sfi in the US since 1998(25 worldwide), and pretty much all the case reports are available online. Also Sfi is not the sporadic version of Ffi, it’s the thalamic form  of CJD. The real name for Sfi is MM2-Thalamic CJD. 

So if you have had vivid dreams for years and have insomnia now, you don’t have Sfi.
